text:
incident-bot: ALERT: detected high error rates and DNS failures for traffic egressing azure-swedencentral -> on-prem via ExpressRoute. Symptoms: elevated TCP RSTs, intermittent DNS SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN for internal hostnames, p95 latency spike. Auto-escalating to oncall.

emma (eng-sre): I'm seeing a lot of TCP resets in the proxy logs targeting the private gateway prefixes. Example: connection to 10.48.9.12 times out then RST. Repro with curl to internal control plane endpoints.

raj (infra): Quick context: our BGP session with the ExpressRoute circuit is flapping routes intermittently. I've pulled bgp updates and there's frequent path changes to different Azure nexthops (10.200.x.x / 10.201.x.x). This looks like route convergence in the region fabric.

olivia (oncall): I'm taking oncall. Paging Azure support and touching base with customer-sre. @matt can you confirm which customers are seeing impact so we can set comms? :rotating_light:

matt (customer-sre): Three customers opened alerts via support: two on Dedicated+Private, one on a private VNet-peered deployment. Telemetry: request success rate for swedencentral private routes down ~20% in the last 12m. Embeddings ingestion and a few short-lived sync jobs failing. No indication of data corruption, only connectivity/timeouts.

simon (network): Ran a traceroute from our egress probe in swedencentral -> onprem. See hops alternate between two different Azure next-hops, last hop alternates but TTLs stable. Output:
```
traceroute to onprem-gw (203.0.113.5), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  1.0 ms  0.8 ms  0.9 ms
 2  10.200.1.1  8.6 ms  9.0 ms  9.1 ms
 3  10.200.2.5  40.2 ms  *  41.0 ms
 4  10.201.3.9  80.5 ms  78.9 ms  79.2 ms
 5  203.0.113.5  120.6 ms  *  119.8 ms
```
Pattern: hop 3/4 flip-flops between 10.200.2.5 and 10.201.3.9.

emma (eng-sre): Also seeing DNS anomalies for internal service names: UDP queries to our private DNS sometimes get SERVFAIL. Switching DNS to TCP temporarily on probes returns correct answers, which implies packet loss on the UDP path likely due to asymmetric routing.

raj (infra): Proposed mitigation options:
- Option A: Apply routing policy override to steer swedencentral private egress to westeurope edge (egress_region:westeurope) until Azure stabilizes.
- Option B: Suppress problematic BGP communities if Azure supports it (ask support).
- Option C: Keep trying to ride it out (not great for customers).
Which one do we want to execute?

olivia (oncall): I vote for Option A for immediate customer relief. We need a quick rollback plan. @emma can you push the override and monitor? I'll update status.

emma (eng-sre): Pushing a temporary override to smart-router now for tenant selectors matching `region:swedencentral && connection:expressroute`. Config snippet I'm applying: 
```json
{
  "selector": "region:swedencentral && connection:expressroute",
  "egress_override": "westeurope",
  "ttl": 14400,
  "reason": "swedencentral egress instability - temporary reroute"
}
```
Applying...

az-support-bot: Azure support case created: INC12345678. Azure engineer assigned, initial note: "We are seeing intermittent route convergence in the Sweden central peering fabric affecting ExpressRoute customer circuits. Investigating chassis-level flaps."

matt (customer-sre): Posted incident on status page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2001002345 - severity: partial outage for private-connected workloads in swedencentral. Messaging: customers may see timeouts/5xx, we are routing around issue and will provide updates.

raj (infra): Route override accepted by router and advertised. Monitoring for health metrics now.

simon (network): New traceroute after override shows stable path via westeurope edge:
```
traceroute to onprem-gw (203.0.113.5) via westeurope:
 1  10.0.0.1  1.0 ms
 2  10.150.1.1  18.2 ms
 3  10.150.2.9  35.4 ms
 4  203.0.113.5  90.2 ms
```
No flip-flop observed.

emma (eng-sre): Service success rate back up to ~98% for impacted tenants. DNS SERVFAILs subsided when forcing TCP and now appear stable via the new path. Rolling the policy to all affected tenant selectors.

olivia (oncall): Good. I'll mark as mitigated once Azure confirms root cause and we have a timeline for full mitigation. @product-ops please own postmortem and RCA with Azure details.

product-ops: Acknowledged. Scheduling follow-up meeting and postmortem doc. We'll include timeline, mitigation steps, and recommendations (improve route monitoring and automatic failover thresholds).

az-support-bot: Azure update: "Root cause: transient route flap in peering fabric causing next-hop churn. Engineering applied fabric-level stabilization patches. Monitoring continues."

matt (customer-sre): Customers notified. No evidence of data loss, only transient connectivity. Will monitor support tickets for regressions.

olivia (oncall): :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated via egress reroute at 2001002440. Leaving channel to Raj/Emma for cleanup and follow-ups. I'll update the incident channel and set a postmortem owner/time.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated at 2001002440 - active watch period started. Please add any logs/notes to the incident doc and close when RCA is complete.

emma (eng-sre): Leaving notes: temporary override TTL set to 4h. After Azure confirms, we'll either remove override or re-point to native path. Collecting GRPC logs and DNS probes for the postmortem.

raj (infra): I'll coordinate with Azure engineering for the RCA details and confirm if we need a longer-term routing policy for swedencentral.

simon (network): Verified latency and success metrics; no more flip-flop.

product-ops: Postmortem meeting scheduled for tomorrow 11:00 CET. Adding agenda: detection improvements, auto-failover criteria, and customer comms cadence.

matt (customer-sre): Thanks everyone. I'll keep the status updated and close customer notifications after the RCA.

olivia (oncall): handing off to infra for follow-up. Closing oncall rotation. :handshake:
